subtitle: Lesson 52 · PostgreSQL Deep Dive for T-SQL Developers

caption: Three pieces don't translate literally: IDENTITY, TOP, and ISNULL.

eyebrow: Decision 1: IDENTITY becomes GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY
code:
-- Modern, standard-compliant PostgreSQL (preferred)
CREATE TABLE customers (
  customer_id INT GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  phone VARCHAR(20)
);

-- Older PostgreSQL-specific shortcut, still common
-- customer_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY
caption: SERIAL still works -- GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY is the modern choice.

eyebrow: Decision 2 & 3: TOP moves and becomes LIMIT; ISNULL becomes COALESCE
code:
-- PostgreSQL
SELECT customer_id, customer_name,
  COALESCE(phone, 'No phone on file') AS phone_display
FROM customers
ORDER BY customer_id DESC
LIMIT 10;
caption: LIMIT moves to the end. PostgreSQL has no ISNULL -- COALESCE replaces it.
